items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: he also had another wonderful trombone player, Red Stewart. He and Jack alternated between the years.

ctx.x: Something else I remember reading about it, maybe you can talk to Jack, that was Doc Ross's band, when they called it the Cowboy Band, in Los Angeles. Yeah. Did you all have to wear any outfits or anything to look like that?

I did. When I joined the Doc Ross Band in California in 1925, they were playing at Solomon's Penny Danstree Lodge. This was an unbelievable place. Huge ballroom. Paid a penny a dance. They had three bands. One was Ranger Ross, Texas Cowboy Band, direct from Texas. And, then, we played the popular music. We played the popular music. Mosby's Dixieland Blue Bloys with a black band, which was fabulous, looking back. I mean, Jack and I used to go over and stand by the stand, the bandstand, just to get to hear them.…
Well, did they, did you, were you on that famous parade? When the horseback?
